questions.question: Using the election results of July 1932, November 1932 and March 1933, describe the level of Nazi support and explain which groups tended to vote Nazi.
questions.expected_answer: July 1932: 37,3 percent and 230 seats, the largest party; November 1932: 33,1 percent and 196 seats; March 1933: 43,9 percent and 288 seats in an election held under terror. The Nazis never won a majority in a free election. Their support was strongest among Protestant, rural and small-town voters, farmers, shopkeepers, white-collar workers, civil servants, the young and new voters, and those fearing communism; weaker among Catholics and organised industrial workers.

questions.question: Explain how Hitler became chancellor in January 1933 and why the conservatives' plan failed.
questions.expected_answer: After the failure of Papen's and Schleicher's governments, Papen and other conservatives persuaded Hindenburg to appoint Hitler chancellor on 30 January 1933 in a coalition with only three Nazis, believing they could use his mass support and control him. The plan failed because the Nazis controlled the interior ministry and police, Hitler was ruthless, the Reichstag fire gave a pretext for emergency powers, and Hindenburg died in 1934.

questions.question: Explain how the Reichstag Fire Decree and the Enabling Act turned Germany into a dictatorship, and name three steps of coordination that followed.
questions.expected_answer: The decree of 28 February 1933 suspended civil liberties, allowing arrests without charge of Communists and others. The Enabling Act of 23 March 1933, passed 444 to 94 with Communists excluded and under SA intimidation, let the government make laws without the Reichstag. Coordination followed: state governments replaced, trade unions abolished in May 1933, all parties except the Nazis banned by July 1933, the Gestapo created, the SA leadership purged in June 1934, and Hitler made Führer in August 1934.
